name: Weight Plate Bus Driver
summary: An isolation exercise that holds a weight plate straight out and rotates it side-to-side to challenge the anterior deltoids and shoulder stabilizers.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, or sit upright on a flat bench with your core braced.
Grip the sides of a weight plate at roughly the 9 and 3 o'clock positions.
Raise the plate straight out in front of you to shoulder height with arms extended and a slight, soft bend in the elbows.
steps: Maintaining shoulder height, smoothly rotate the plate like a steering wheel until one hand is directly above the other (12 and 6 o'clock).
Pause momentarily, then reverse the rotation back through center until the opposite hand is on top.
Continue alternating sides smoothly while keeping the arms elevated and torso upright.
instructions.breathing: Breathe in a steady, continuous rhythm throughout the set without holding your breath against the isometric burn.
cues: Keep the plate at eye-to-shoulder height
Turn from the shoulders, not just the wrists
Lock your ribcage down to avoid leaning back

common_faults.fault: Letting the arms drop below shoulder height as fatigue sets in.
common_faults.correction: Use a lighter plate to maintain full shoulder elevation throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Arching the lower back to compensate for shoulder fatigue.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs to keep the pelvis and spine neutral.

common_faults.fault: Excessively bending the elbows into a chest press position.
common_faults.correction: Keep elbows nearly straight with only a soft micro-bend to maximize lever-arm tension on the deltoids.

precautions: Start with light weight plates (5–10 lb / 2.5–5 kg), as the long lever arm places significant demand on shoulder stamina.
